summary: Milestone 2l replaces milestone 2i's authored-command stand-in with the path the game uses. The scene's `Command` token is resolved by 0046aab0 against the 26-row registry at 00e19a70, issued by 0077d600 as MT_COMMAND with flags 1, applied by 00816e30, handed to the weapon director by 0071ecf0, received back as MT_GAMEUNIT_SETCMD by 00721a40's 5Ch arm and pushed into command slot 0 by 008358d0 / 0071e6c0; 00835c70's own arm then latches the ring's ordered pair and the heading through 00835ac0, and 009e1170's AI arm re-applies what it latched every fixed step. Because `cruise` is a latch rather than an order, the ships hold what their ring held, which for this mission is zero: 13 of the 32 created instances author `Cruise` and all 13 stay stopped, and the other 19 author `None`, which resolves to no command class at all. The mission's own orders come from its script rather than from the scene or the AI bindings: `luaStageInit` hands `CreateScript` the name `luaInit`, and that function addresses 21 of the 32 created instances through ten bindings, every one of which is a host record. The x87 precision field is read at run time before Direct3D (53-bit) and at the fixed simulation step (24-bit), which confirms docs/X87_CONTROL_WORD.md's static answer by observation.

mission_script_steps.note: The `CreateScript` binding row of the 560-entry table at 00e0b7b8. Its body registers a script object; the executable keeps the name it was handed and nothing else. usn_2_java.lua's `luaStageInit` hands it `luaInit`.

Fixed-step fan-out row 8, the other. With both recorded, the executable calls the named global once with one fresh table on the frame the mission enters state 0dh.

The per-entity `thisTable` slot builder and its caller 0077e830. The executable builds 32 slots with the recovered `ID`, `Dead` and `Ptr` fields, and assigns each one the installed `VehicleClass` row as its `Class`, which is the field a per-kind setter adds later through 00b675d0. The native `Ptr` is lightuserdata(entity); this process has no entity object, so the slot carries the entity's own id as a light pointer and nothing dereferences it.

With the slots built, the entity tail of the 19 entity-returning rows can push thisTable[key] instead of the nil arm. Only `FindEntity` is resolved, 33 times: 00925a90's own lookup is a record and the executable walks the created instances instead. Every other entity-returning row resolves its subject from game state this process does not own and keeps the nil arm.

precision.claim: The CRT startup sets the x87 precision field to 53 bits and nothing in the image changes it again; the Direct3D 9 device is created without D3DCREATE_FPU_PRESERVE, so d3d9.dll is expected to drop the field to 24 bits for the life of the device.
precision.reader: _controlfp_s(&value, 0, 0) & _MCW_PC, once in WinMain before Direct3D exists and once on the first fixed simulation step
precision.note: This closes uncertainty 1 of that document, which recorded the 24-bit write as documented API behaviour of d3d9.dll rather than as an observation. Neither read changes any arithmetic.

corrections.was: docs/GAME_EXECUTABLE.md milestone 2h: `the `Command` property, which all 32 author as `Cruise``, and milestone 2i's stand-in, which gave all 32 an order-ring order of throttle 1 and rudder 0.
corrections.is: 13 of the 32 created instances author `Cruise`; the other 19 carry `None`, the value `properties Command` in universe/library/commandunit.props declares as its default. `None` is value 1 of that file's `enum CommandType` and is not a command class, so 0046aab0's first-match walk over the registry at 00e19a70 finds nothing and ends those records at 0046ab13.
corrections.evidence: The run's per-unit command table: DeRuyter, Java, Electra, Houston, Alden, John1, John2, John3, Exeter, Perth, Encounter, Jupiter and Witte resolve to ordinal 16; Kortenaer and the eighteen Japanese ships resolve to nothing. universe/library/commandunit.props lines 1-31.

corrections.was: docs/CRUISE_COMMAND.md: `Both producers of a `Cruise` with no target agree exactly ... a descriptor whose kind is 0 and whose position is the read-only zero vector at 00F87574.`
corrections.is: Only the Lua producer builds a zero-vector descriptor. The scene queue's targetless branch fills the descriptor with the OWNER's own world position: 0046abb7, 0046abc5 and 0046abd8 load owner+fch, owner+100h and owner+104h into [ESP+20h], [ESP+24h] and [ESP+28h], with the kind byte clear at 0046abef and position_valid set to 1 at 0046abe0. The two producers agree on the command object and the flags, not on the descriptor. Nothing about `cruise` depends on it, because the latch reads the ring and not the descriptor.
corrections.evidence: Raw disassembly 0046aba0-0046abf3 against the disk bytes, and the same branch in src/scene_deferred_refs.cpp, which already wrote the owner position.

corrections.was: This packet's brief: `run the mission's AI groups from their scripted AICreate/AISetCommand bindings (the mission script calls them at stage init)`.
corrections.is: No installed mission script calls them. A scan of the 299 `.lua` files under Scripts/missions finds zero call sites for AICreate, AICreateGroup, AISetCommand, AIEnable, AIEnableGrouping, AIMergeGroups, AIGetGroupInfo, AIReloadGlobals, AIGetTargetWeight and AISetQuickSpawnTargetPos; only the four tuning bindings appear (AISetHintWeight 32 files, AISetSpawnSceneUnitsWeightMul 31, AISetTargetWeight 29, AISetDefendResourcePercent 6). usn_2_java.lua calls no AI binding at all. What issues this mission's orders is the `Navigator*` family, from the `luaInit` function its stage init hands to CreateScript.
corrections.evidence: The corpus scan above, and docs/LUA_BINDING_AI.md's own `What the installed scripts reach` section, which says the same thing.

corrections.was: docs/GAME_EXECUTABLE.md milestone 2i: `Every unit's authored `Command` is `Cruise`. What that token means is not recovered ... The executable turns it into one order-ring order of throttle 1 and rudder 0 through the recovered 00816a40`.
corrections.is: Superseded. The token is recovered and it writes no ring: 00835ac0 stores three fields on the weapon director at +243h, +244h and +248h, and 00825f20 refills the ring from unit+0fc4h / unit+0fdch under the unit+61h gate, from a producer that is still unread. The executable no longer writes a ring for an authored command, and the mission's 13 `Cruise` ships therefore stay where the scene placed them.
corrections.evidence: The 2l run: 13 units latched, 0 with a non-zero thrust, total path 196.55 m of which 196.54 m is the controlled unit under --order.

corrections.was: docs/X87_CONTROL_WORD.md uncertainty 1: `The 24-bit write is performed by d3d9.dll. It is documented behaviour ... and no run log was taken`.
corrections.is: Observed. The executable reads _controlfp_s(&v, 0, 0) & _MCW_PC twice in the same run: 0x00010000 (53-bit) in WinMain before Direct3D is created, and 0x00020000 (24-bit) on the first fixed simulation step. The static reading was right.

follow_up_packets: unit_autopilot_pair: unit+61h, unit+0fc4h, unit+0fdch and the writer that carries the AI controller block at [state]+8 into them. It is the one hop between a latched cruise and a moving ship, and it is why 13 ships hold station under a command the reconstruction runs end to end.

cruise_speed_setting: *(unit+73ch)+24h and +28h, the commanded speed 009e1170 would divide by 0080fc30's reference speed. Its enable is read at three sites and cleared at one; nothing writes +24h through a direct displacement.

mission_navigator_bindings: 008a2f20 NavigatorMoveToRange, 008a30d0 NavigatorAttackMove, 00899d10 JoinFormation, 0089a8b0 SetFireTarget, 008a3cd0 and 008a3b10. They are what usn_2_java.lua's own luaInit calls on 21 of its 32 ships, and every one of them is a host record today.
mission_script_manager: 00898750 CreateScript, 00888230 and 00929460, so a script object is registered and run by the game's own scheduler rather than called once by the executable.
ship_ai_state_machine: 00d21598, 009f3dd0 and the rest of the state class family, so 009e1170 runs where the game runs it and the moveto / follow / stop states exist at all.

lua_binding_return_values: the first binding whose return value a shipped script consumes stops the script. luaRnd is the one this mission hits; a run that wants luaInit to finish needs those rows to answer.
